subject: physics
title: Centre of gravity and stability
key_idea: The centre of gravity is the point where the whole weight of an object seems to act. An object is more stable with a low centre of gravity and a wide base. It topples when a vertical line from its centre of gravity falls outside its base.

blocks.text: Every part of an object has weight. We can treat all of that weight as one force acting from a single point.

items.meaning: The point where the whole weight of an object seems to act.
A thin, flat sheet of material.

items: The weight of an object acts **through** its centre of gravity, vertically downwards.
For a regular object of uniform material, the centre of gravity is at its geometric centre.
For an irregular object it must be found by experiment.
The centre of gravity does not have to be inside the object. A ring has its centre of gravity in the hole.
Centre of gravity is the point where all the weight seems to act.
Weight acts through the centre of gravity.

sections.heading: Finding the centre of gravity of a lamina

blocks.text: A freely hanging lamina comes to rest with its centre of gravity directly below the point it hangs from. A plumb line shows the vertical.

items.text: Make three small holes near the edge of the lamina.
Hang the lamina from a pin in a clamp, through one hole, so that it swings freely.
Hang a plumb line from the same pin. Wait until both are still.
Mark two points on the lamina where the string passes. Draw a line through them with a ruler.
Hang the lamina from each of the other holes and draw the lines.
The lines cross at the centre of gravity.

items: Two lines are enough, and the third checks the result.
A uniform metre ruler balances on a pivot at its centre of gravity. The balance point is the centre of gravity.

diagram.alt: A sequencing activity. Put the steps for finding the centre of gravity of a lamina in the correct order.
diagram.prompt: Put the steps for finding the centre of gravity of an irregular lamina in order.
steps: Make small holes near the edge of the lamina.
Hang the lamina from a pin through one hole.
Hang a plumb line from the same pin.
Draw a line along the plumb line on the lamina.
The centre of gravity is where the lines cross.

items: A hanging lamina has its centre of gravity vertically below the pin.
Plumb-line lines from different holes cross at the centre of gravity.

blocks.text: Stability is how hard an object is to topple. It depends on where the centre of gravity is and how wide the base is.

items: If you tilt an object, its centre of gravity moves with it.
While a vertical line down from the centre of gravity stays **inside the base**, the weight turns the object back.
When the line moves **outside the base**, the weight turns the object over and it topples.
A low centre of gravity and a wide base mean the object has to tilt further before it topples.
A ship carries its heaviest containers at the bottom, so its centre of gravity is lower.
A tall, thin transmitter without wires is very unstable. A small tilt puts the centre of gravity outside the base.

diagram.alt: A sorting activity. Sort the features into those that make an object more stable and those that make it less stable.
diagram.prompt: Does each feature make an object more stable or less stable?

items.text: Heavy load kept at the bottom
Heavy load kept at the top

items: An object topples when its centre of gravity is no longer above its base.
A low centre of gravity and a wide base give greater stability.

checks.q: State what is meant by centre of gravity.
checks.a: The point where the whole weight of the object seems to act.

checks.q: Describe how a plumb line is used to find the centre of gravity of an irregular lamina.
checks.a: Hang the lamina freely from a pin through a hole and hang a plumb line from the same pin. Draw the vertical line on the lamina. Repeat from another hole. The centre of gravity is where the lines cross.

checks.q: Explain why a bus with its heavy luggage at the bottom is less likely to topple.
checks.a: The centre of gravity is lower, so the bus has to tilt further before the centre of gravity is outside the base.

worked_example.question: The containers with the greatest mass are loaded near the bottom of a ship. State and explain the effect on the stability of the ship of loading the containers in this way.
answer_points: The centre of gravity is lower.
So the ship is more stable.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the lower centre of gravity and one for the effect on stability.

worked_example.question: A metal block sits on top of a wooden block and is held stationary by a force F. The weight of the metal block acts through point G. Give the name of point G.
answer_points: Centre of gravity (centre of mass is also accepted).
worked_example.tip: The weight of a body always acts through its centre of gravity.
